term: activity-sensitive linguistic practice or language game
definition: An activity with purposes, participant roles and rules distinguishing competent linguistic moves. The purposes and rules supply the role used to assess competent moves; whether learning that role is necessary for understanding actual expressions is the separate OPEN analyst thesis. Such specificity does not define a practice as insulated from shared evidence, make every assertion true, or make its rules categorically binding.
note: Stipulative analyst sense, attribution DEFERRED; actual instantiation remains OPEN. Fideism.Practice supplies a narrower reusable move/standard interface but is not identified with all such activities. The sharp fideist cut-off and Phillips readings remain separate existing positions; docs/wittgenstein.md.
